title: Ramp and Rollout Capacity Slate
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a compact operational tracker that converts a high-level roadmap into per-week capacity budgets, owner lanes, and KPI microplans for staged rollouts. Intended for product ops -> release engineering -> SRE coordination during the 6-week ramp window. Use this as the single-source sprint view for capacity allocations and decision thresholds.

How to use (quick):
- Step 0: Pick the rollout cohort (alpha / beta / general).
- Step 1: Note target traffic % and expected QPS for week 0..6.
- Step 2: Map infra capacity (GPUs, replica targets, pool headroom) to the week.
- Step 3: Assign an owner for each lane (traffic, infra, observability, QA, CS).
- Step 4: Fill KPI microplans (primary metric, guardrail metric, threshold, action).
- Step 5: Watch the escalation column each day; update status and incident links.

Summary table (example rows) - copy into main spreadsheet:
Week | Cohort | Target % | Est QPS | GPU cap (v100-eq) | Owners (traffic/infra/obs/qa/cs) | Primary KPI | Guardrail | Threshold | Action if breached
W0   | alpha  | 0.5%     | 5      | 0.5               | Evan / Tariq / Lena / Priya / Maya    | p95 latency | error rate | p95>350ms or error>0.5% | rollback to canary route + page SRE
W1   | alpha  | 2%       | 20     | 1                 | Evan / Tariq / Lena / Priya / Maya    | tokens/s    | quota-exhaust | tokens/s drop>10% | scale pool + throttle low-priority routes
W3   | beta   | 15%      | 150    | 2.5               | Priya / Raj / Lena / QA-team / CS-lead | user success rate | latency p95 | success<97% | run hotspot eval, pause GA expansion

Capacity knobs explained:
- GPU cap (v100-eq): conservative equivalent for planning. Use infra-estimates for instance mix (A100/MI300) in notes column.
- Pool headroom: percentage of extra reserved capacity to absorb bursts (recommended default 20% during ramp).
- Warmup windows: plan 30–90m warmups for heavy models before shifting traffic.

KPI microplans (per owner lane) - short templates you can copy into tickets:
- Traffic Owner microplan: monitor daily traffic ingestion vs forecast; maintain routing fallback ready; success = within ±10% of forecast. Escalate if variance >20% for 2 consecutive hours.
- Infra Owner microplan: keep GPU utilization 40–70% on primary pools; failover pool <70% utilization; action: auto-scale policy toggle + manual scale if >80% for 10m.
- Observability Owner microplan: ensure p95, p50, error-rate, and cold-start charts emit 1m alarms; validate tracing sampling on canary.
- QA Owner microplan: run 2 full smoke prompt-sets after every infra change; report quality regressions to product with examples and eval IDs.
- CS Owner microplan: coordinate early user comms for alpha cohort; collect NPS + friction notes daily and post into release channel.

Decision thresholds (examples):
- Soft guardrail: single metric breach for <30m — alert on-call and watch.
- Hard guardrail: sustained breach for >30m or concurrent two metrics breach — trigger rollback plan A.
- Emergency: cascade failure (high error + high latency + quota failure) — run full rollback to previous model and page on-call SRE.

Risks & mitigation notes:
- Unexpected model memory growth on long sequences: mitigate by limiting max_seq for ramped cohorts and enabling KV cache eviction strategy.
- Burst traffic from integrations: pre-configure burst credits and verify quota gating.
- Eval drift: keep a small fixed prompt-set for live quality watermarking; if >2pt drop on core metric, stop expansion.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Bench ips for models and sequence lengths for the cohorts. Link bench sheet.
- [ ] Create canary route and test cold-start latency on new infra.
- [ ] Confirm alert thresholds in console and set aliases.
- [ ] Lock burn rate and budget owner.
- [ ] Schedule daily check-in channel (15m) for W0-W2.

Post-rollout telemetry & debrief prompts:
- Capture top-5 contributors to token cost delta and annotate with prompt types.
- Weekly debrief: owners add 1–2 sentences about what surprised them, what was expected, and immediate follow-ups.

Notes / open questions:
- Do we want a generic 5% safety headroom for GA rollouts or vary by model family? (ask infra + product pricing)
- Is there appetite to pre-warm KV caches automatically when moving from alpha→beta? (SRE cost implications)

Recent changes log:
- 2026-01-15: Added explicit warmup window guidance per model size (Priya)
- 2026-01-28: Updated decision thresholds to include dual-metric hard guardrail (Evan)
